summary: A developer can seek conditional use approval in the Commercial Business or Industrial Business district. The township requires a site of at least 50 acres.
evidence: Data Center shall be permitted by conditional use

summary: The setback covers the data center and its accessory uses where the property line directly borders residential use or residential zoning.
evidence: setback 150 feet from any property line

thresholds.context: Applies along directly adjoining residential use or residentially zoned property.

summary: The developer must study outdoor equipment noise and submit a second study six months after the center reaches full operation.
evidence: six months after the Data Center is fully operational

summary: The developer must show the public utility approved its application for service. Public water and sewer must meet the proposed use.
evidence: an application for service is approved

summary: The county allows centers below 50 kilowatts in its Light Industrial and General Industrial districts. The change covers unincorporated land; cities set their own zoning.
locator: Nov. 13 adoption notice, describing changes effective Nov. 10
authority: Boulder County Board of County Commissioners
evidence: data centers are permitted under 50 kilowatts

thresholds.context: Light Industrial and General Industrial districts in the unincorporated county

summary: For qualifying data center permits, Pennsylvania DEP requires proof that the project fits the local comprehensive plan and has received the applicable local zoning and subdivision approvals.
locator: Executive Order 2026-05, DEP directives, p. 4, paragraph (b)
authority: Pennsylvania Governor and Department of Environmental Protection
evidence: received all local or municipal approvals under the applicable subdivision and zoning ordinance

summary: A developer proposing work that could harm coastal resources must apply for a land use permit unless the law exempts the work.
evidence: shall apply for a land use permit, except where specifically exempted by law

summary: If the project falls under coastal management jurisdiction, the developer must obtain written approval before work starts. Major siting applications require a public hearing.
locator: DCRM, The Permitting Process; opening guidance and Public Comment
evidence: All major sitings require a public hearing

summary: The territory reviews proposed development in its designated first-tier coastal zone. Check the parcel boundary before assuming coastal review applies.
locator: DPNR, Coastal Zone Permitting, opening paragraph
authority: Department of Planning and Natural Resources
evidence: assess all proposed development in the first tier

summary: Guam accepts building permit applications at the Business License and Permit Center at Public Works in Upper Tumon. The center brings together land management, fire and other reviewing agencies.
locator: Guam Development Guidebook, Business License and Permit Center
evidence: applying for building permits

summary: Before approving a land-use application for a new large data center, a municipal or county land-use authority must notify the Division of Water Rights, Division of Water Quality and any relevant water provider. The definition combines at least 75 acre-feet in annual withdrawals with at least 10,000 square feet and qualifying IT use, infrastructure, ownership/lease and parcel tests. New means starting operations on or after July 1, 2026.
evidence: the relevant water provider, if any

thresholds.context: All statutory facility and ownership or lease conditions must also apply.
All statutory size, use, utility infrastructure and withdrawal conditions also apply.

summary: Starting July 1, 2026, operators of qualifying new large data centers must give the provider written consumption estimates and report project water information to the division 90 to 360 days before construction.
evidence: at least 90 days, but no sooner than 360 days

summary: For the QTS property, the development agreement provides for site-plan entitlement for the full campus and allows an excavation permit before site-plan approval. Building plans go to third-party reviewers; review fees are paid to the City. This is a parcel-specific agreement, not a citywide exemption.
locator: QTS development agreement, Project Approvals exhibit: Site Plan, Excavation and Building Permit Approval
evidence: Site work permit can be obtained prior to Site Plan Approval

summary: Ordinance 37-26 pauses new and pending city applications for six months from effectiveness unless changed. Any one trigger suffices: gross floor area over 100,000 square feet, planned or actual demand over 75 MW, at least 5,000 servers, or cooling/operational water use of at least 50 gallons per minute. Exceptions cover minor work at existing non-hyperscale facilities, emergency safety work and city IT. Adopted September 21, 2026; effective upon publication, not independently dated here.
authority: City of Dubuque, official code publisher
evidence: Server Count of 5,000 or more servers

summary: Iowa DNR requires a water withdrawal permit when an entity takes at least 25,000 gallons from surface water or groundwater in any 24-hour period. A center buying municipal water generally uses supply covered by the utility’s permit.
evidence: 25,000 gallons or more

summary: For construction disturbing at least one acre, obtain coverage under General Permit No. 2 and maintain a pollution prevention plan through stabilization.
evidence: disturbing one or more acres

summary: Surface-water disposal of cooling blowdown requires an NPDES permit. Discharge into a city sewer instead invokes local pretreatment requirements.
evidence: local municipal pretreatment ordinances

summary: Madison reports its adopted one-year moratorium prevents zoning approvals and, consequently, building and occupancy permits for new principal-use data or telecommunications centers above 10,000 square feet. The stated end is January 24, 2027 unless replaced sooner by a new ordinance. The city’s October 2026 zoning framework is a draft.
authority: City of Madison, Department of Planning and Community and Economic Development
locator: Temporary Data Center Moratorium: What Does the Moratorium Do?; Frequently Asked Questions
evidence: over 10,000 square feet in floor area

summary: Atlanta prohibits new data centers within half a mile of a MARTA rail station or future bus rapid transit stop covered by the zoning amendment.
evidence: within half a mile of MARTA train stations or future Bus Rapid Transit stops
locator: Plan A (adopted city comprehensive plan), printed p. 75 / PDF p. 122, 24-O-1222

thresholds.context: Covered rail stations or future bus rapid transit stops; city zoning amendment 24-O-1222

summary: Atlanta prohibits new data centers in the Beltline Overlay District. Use the mapped district boundary to check a parcel.
evidence: out of the Beltline Overlay District
locator: Plan A, printed p. 75 / PDF p. 122, 24-O-1218

summary: Aurora bars evaporative chillers that use potable water. The restriction applies to data centers seeking conditional use approval.
evidence: Evaporative chillers utilizing potable water

summary: A data center may use at most 0.2 liters of potable building water per kilowatt-hour consumed by its IT equipment.
evidence: no more than two tenths (0.2).

thresholds.context: Potable building water per kWh consumed by IT equipment

summary: Measure from the nearest part of the equipment yard to the property line of a home, hospital or educational use. A later neighboring use does not undo an existing conditional approval.
evidence: located within one thousand (1,000’) feet of

thresholds.context: Existing residential, hospital or educational use

summary: A third-party engineer must model water consumption and water quality. The report covers supply sources, average and peak demand, and cooling and water reuse plans.
evidence: A Water Consumption and Quality Modeling

summary: The first application must include a week of baseline noise measurements. A separate acoustical study must model compliance with the applicable limits.
evidence: a continuous weeklong period

summary: Santa Clara requires structural noise controls on exterior cooling fans and equipment. The city’s community development director decides whether measures such as baffles or acoustic louvers are sufficient.
evidence: structural noise reduction measures for any exterior cooling fans or equipment

summary: Santa Clara requires fully shielded exterior lights that direct light away from adjoining roads and properties.
evidence: cutoff and fully shielded fixtures

summary: Conway’s enacted use table lists both Limited and General data centers as conditional in I-1 and as permitted (X) in I-3. The General designation is a secondary use and also conditional across the other listed districts; the Limited designation’s remaining cells are blank. Both definitions expressly cover digital asset mining.
locator: O-23-72 §1, permitted use table and §1302 definitions (pp. 1–2)
evidence: Data Center (Limited)

summary: For a data-center conditional use application, submit building plans, a noise study and a noise attenuation plan. Planning and Development staff can also request utility-use information.
evidence: Noise Study and a Noise Attenuation Plan

summary: In the county’s General Business (BG) district, data centers require a special use permit. This is county zoning; it is not automatically the rule within Papillion or another municipality.
locator: Zoning Regulations, Resolution 2024-030 (approved 2024-01-23), §20.2.4, General Business district; §40
evidence: 20.2.4 Data Centers.

summary: Data centers are listed among permitted principal uses in the Heavy General Business (BGH) and Light Industrial (IL) districts of the county zoning jurisdiction. District development, overlay and building requirements remain applicable.
evidence: 21.1.7 Data Centers.

summary: In the county zoning jurisdiction, a data-center site plan requires placement in the Critical Digital Infrastructure Overlay Zone and Limited Industrial or General Industrial base zoning. The 2,614-acre overlay is mapped in the Eastalco Community Growth Area. Do not infer approval of a particular parcel or applicability inside the City of Frederick.
locator: Annual Planning Report 2025, p. 8; Bill 25-09 and adopted CDI zoning map amendment
authority: Frederick County Division of Planning and Permitting
evidence: Limited Industrial (LI) or General Industrial (GI)

summary: Lowell identifies its existing data-center property as Light Industrial. Its planning department states that a lawfully pre-existing nonconforming use may continue until a change of use or abandonment for two years. This site guidance does not grant new data centers district-wide permission, and the city describes its permanent zoning rewrite as pending.
locator: Data Centers, Q&A re existing Markley use, MGL Ch 40A §6; district of existing facility
authority: City of Lowell Department of Planning and Development
evidence: Light Industrial (LI) zoning district
